NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using scavenge-air pressure deviation as the primary indicator.  
My departure: A fouling-rate indicator derived from the time-derivative of scavenge-air pressure normalized by turbocharger speed, detecting incipient fouling before pressure drops 8%.  
This works because fouling deposits accumulate nonlinearly, causing accelerating pressure loss; the derivative amplifies early warning.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Fouling-induced pressure loss ∝ (deposit thickness × flow resistance).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = deposit thickness; the mechanism moves it DOWN by early detection (enabling cleaning); this REDUCES flow resistance.  
Magnitude verification: At 8% pressure drop (ΔP/P = 0.08), fouling-rate threshold = 0.008/day (CALCULATED from 10-day warning window).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
(a1) Scavenge-air pressure sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "existing scavenge-air pressure signal")  
(a2) Turbocharger speed sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "existing turbocharger speed signal")  
(a3) Engine load sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "existing engine load signal")  
(b1) Signal processing unit (calculates d(P_scavenge)/dt and normalizes by turbocharger speed)  
(c1) Alarm logic module (triggers when normalized pressure rate > 0.008/day at reference load)  
Reference threshold: 0.008/day (CALCULATED from 10-day warning window and 8% failure threshold)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: SAME (uses existing sensors; no new hardware)  
- Operability: SAME (no operator intervention; automated rate calculation)  
- Maintenance: SAME (no additional maintenance; software update only)  
- Cost class: SAME (no new sensors; only signal processing logic)  
- Operational loss: Zero (early warning prevents efficiency loss)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Log scavenge-air pressure, turbocharger speed, and engine load at 1-hour intervals for 30 days. Pass if: (1) Normalized pressure rate exceeds 0.008/day at least 10 days before any 8% pressure drop, and (2) ≤1 false alarm/year (threshold = 0.008/day).  
Kill criterion: ≥2 false alarms or failure to trigger 10 days before 8% pressure drop.  
Duration: 30 days (covers multiple fouling cycles).  
Validation: Uses ALREADY-RECORDED data from prior fouling events.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Scavenge-air pressure (per problem statement; threshold defines failure).  
Supplement: Normalized pressure rate (derivative) for early warning.
